title: Tshisekedi Launches Three-Month National Dialogue, Excludes M23
detail: President Félix Tshisekedi launched a three-month national dialogue on Aug 28 aimed at peace, national cohesion and state rebuilding, with consultations planned across all 26 provinces before concluding sessions in Kinshasa. He explicitly ruled out participation by armed groups and actors acting on behalf of foreign powers — excluding Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 — saying the process would focus on strengthening state institutions rather than a power-sharing settlement, and that "peace cannot mean impunity" for serious crimes. Participants are to include political parties, civil society, religious and traditional leaders, business representatives, academics, youth and women's groups, and the diaspora. The announcement comes amid rising tension over a June constitutional-referendum bill that opposition coalition C64 says is a vehicle for a Tshisekedi third term.

media.caption: Tshisekedi announces a three-month national dialogue excluding AFC/M23, Aug 28, 2026

confidenceReason: Announcement and its terms are corroborated by three independent outlets across western, eastern and regional poles.

title: Opposition Coalition C64 Rejects Tshisekedi's National Dialogue as "Pretended Consultations"
detail: The Coalition Article 64 (C64) rejected President Tshisekedi's national dialogue on Aug 28, with Martin Fayulu reading a joint statement in Kinshasa branding the process "pretended popular consultations" rather than genuine dialogue. C64 argued the initiative fails to address the country's urgent crises — war, insecurity, health emergencies and social hardship — and instead serves as cover for a constitutional revision aimed at a Tshisekedi third term after 2028, which it said risked the country's territorial integrity. Senator Salomon Idi Kalonda separately called the dialogue "factitious," arguing it distracts from resolving the eastern crisis and restoring national cohesion. C64 reaffirmed its planned nationwide march for Sept 15, 2026 against the constitutional-revision push.

media.caption: C64 coalition leaders, including Martin Fayulu, reject Tshisekedi's proposed national dialogue, Aug 28, 2026

confidenceReason: C64's rejection and its stated rationale are directly reported by Radio Okapi, a Tier-2 MONUSCO-backed outlet with local sourcing; the characterization of the dialogue as a third-term maneuver is C64's contested political framing, not an independently verified fact.
